prompt:
Output exactly one concise, information‑dense caption: a single grammatical sentence composed of comma‑separated short phrases. Produce only that single sentence and nothing else.

Assembly order and allowed tokens (fill slots in this order; place the first subject group + any VERIFIED high‑value prop within the first 6–8 words):
1) Subject group(s) + high‑value prop(s) (0–3 groups, must appear first). If no subject verification → emit plural fallback noun (people/dogs/vehicles).
2) exactly one micro‑action/contact phrase (verified) or conservative part‑near‑object fallback.
3) fine class token (verified) or dataset lexicon fallback.
4) clothing / clear pose / orientation (only if verified).
5) up to two nearby anchors/signage (only if verified; otherwise use compact positional lexicon token).
6) cropping/foreground token (only if depth verified).
Always emit only the specified token for any slot; if verification fails for a slot, substitute the explicit allowed fallback and continue.

Multi‑signal verification (tiered evidence)
For every verification gate compute evidence_set = {geometry, segmentation mask, detector_confidence, contact_confidence, motion_confidence, OCR_confidence, saliency_score, textspot_confidence}. Treat confirmations with three confidence bands:
- HIGH verified: any single evidence ≥ high threshold → allow full VERIFIED emission.
- MEDIUM verified: two complementary evidences ≥ medium threshold (e.g., detector_conf≥0.70 and saliency high OR contact_conf≥0.50 and motion_conf≥0.60) → allow a controlled low‑risk descriptor or detector‑verified emission per slot rules.
- LOW/unverified: otherwise → require strict lexicon fallback.
(Implementors: thresholds are fixed numerics in the pipeline; the captioner uses the band labels, not raw numbers.)

Count verification (digits and counts)
- Emit a digit only when Count is HIGH verified by geometry/segmentation OR when detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70 (detector‑verified). If neither → use plural lexicon fallback (people/dogs/vehicles/group of people). Do not append meta qualifiers; use the digit directly.

Micro‑action / contact rules
- Emit a micro‑action only when HIGH verified OR when combined evidence (contact_conf≥0.50 AND motion_conf≥0.60 or hand_detector+saliency agree) → use exact template: "left|right [hand|foot|part] [strong‑verb] [object]" (example: "right hand holding woven basket"). Motion verbs allowed only with verified motion evidence.
- If micro‑action is MEDIUM verified → allow a restrained action or detector‑verified verb only from a controlled short list; if not, emit conservative fallback: "[part] near [object]" (example: "right hand near woven basket").
- Never use hedging words ("probably", "maybe") in the final caption.

Fine‑class & cue pairs
- Emit a fine class (bicycle, motorbike/scooter, vendor/produce stand, ladder, performer, etc.) only when HIGH verified (classifier_conf≥0.60 OR cue‑pair satisfied) or when MEDIUM verified allow one of the controlled detector labels. Otherwise use dataset lexicon fallback: storefront, painted metal shutter, two‑wheeled vehicle, woven basket, cart, minivan, marquee.

OCR / signage policy (quote only when strongly verified)
- Quote exact text only when OCR_quote_verified HIGH (OCR_confidence ≥ 0.65 AND text_bbox_area and contrast meet thresholds; exception for short marquee ≤3 words with OCR_confidence ≥ 0.60). If OCR_quote_verified HIGH → quote exact text (counts toward length).
- If OCR_confidence is MEDIUM (≈0.50–0.65) AND text_bbox_area or saliency is large → emit a controlled low‑risk descriptor from the allowed set (e.g., "large red sign upper right", "marquee above entrance", "three red rectangular signs upper right"). Do NOT invent characters or partial text.
- If OCR low/unverified → emit compact positional fallback tokens (storefront behind, marquee behind, painted metal shutter).

High‑value anchor checklist
- Attempt verification of anchors in priority order: marquee/storefront, corrugated metal shutter, flagpole, red rectangular signs, ladder, bicycle/two‑wheeled vehicle, guitar/amp case, boats/canopies. If an anchor is unverified, use the prescribed lexicon fallback (e.g., "storefront behind", "flagpole left", "red rectangular sign upper right"). Emit at most two anchor tokens.

Depth, cropping, occlusion
- Emit "foreground"/"background" or "partially cropped at [top|bottom|left|right]" only when depth/cropping is HIGH verified by segmentation or bbox area ratios. Otherwise omit these tokens.

Saliency tie‑breaking
- When multiple VERIFIED candidates compete, prefer tokens with higher saliency: text → face → large color patch/prop → clothing. Use saliency to choose between equally verified anchors or subject groups.

Pruning, compression, and length control
- Target caption length: 10–14 words; hard cap 18 words. Allow up to 20 words only when an exact quoted text string is emitted or two HIGH VERIFIED fine classes are present.
- Before pruning, compress adjective chains into compact noun phrases (e.g., "rustic wooden facade" rather than several separate adjectives). Then, if still over cap, iteratively remove descriptors in this exact priority: lighting/reflection → object state/material → background. NEVER remove HIGH VERIFIED discriminative props, micro‑actions, or fine classes (slots 1–3).
- Maintain a simple token budget while assembling: accept a token only if the estimated cumulative length remains ≤ hard cap; otherwise compress/prune per above.

Allowed lexicon and low‑risk descriptor examples (use only these forms when fallbacks required)
- Dataset lexicon fallbacks: storefront, painted metal shutter, two‑wheeled vehicle, woven basket, cart, minivan, marquee, group of people.
- Low‑risk signage descriptors (MEDIUM OCR): "large red sign upper right", "marquee above entrance", "three red rectangular signs upper right", "storefront behind".
- Anchor fallbacks: "storefront behind", "flagpole left", "marquee above", "painted metal shutter".

Anti‑hallucination absolute rules
- Never invent brand names, quoted text, partial words, celebrity names, ages, emotions, intentions, or unsupported attributes. Do not output hedges. If uncertainty prevents a verified token, use the controlled fallback lexicon above.

Preferred micro‑template shapes (use these shapes when slots allow)
- Examples the caption should prefer to match to verified tokens:
  - "1 woman center foreground, right hand holding woven basket of oranges, storefront behind."
  - "two dogs left foreground, small white dog jumping at car passenger window, woman leaning out."
  - "1 person right foreground, standing by two‑wheeled vehicle with visible pedals and chain, metal shutter behind."
  - "many dancers center foreground, line of red/gold sequined costumes, marquee behind."

Final emission rule
- Execute the verification steps in order, choose HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW bands per multi‑signal evidence, fill assembly slots deterministically with VERIFIED or fallback tokens, compress/prune to meet length budget, and output exactly one comma‑separated grammatical sentence and nothing else.
